statuses.title: Make the linear-FFT safety fallback effective for zero-tail PMFs
statuses.note: Pre-remediation (79c916e3 fft.rs:222-231) any oversized composition silently fell back to a circular FFT whose aliasing was only 'bounded by the Chernoff tail budget' - vacuous when the budget was zero. statuses.title: Reconcile negative-infinity mass in asymmetric PLD metrics
statuses.note: OPQ-181. The audited code is verbatim unchanged: pmf_beta (symmetric) still seeds cdf_y[0] with negative_infinity_mass (metrics.rs:216) while pmf_beta_asymmetric/pmf_beta_symmetrized still drop it via clean_probs renormalization with the very comments the audit quoted ('No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization', metrics.rs:297,306). git diff 79c916e3..4b13d82 on metrics.rs shows only the infinity_mass() helper and test-signature churn; no commit in the window touches the asymmetric beta path and no beta/delta-correspondence test on an amplified PLD (the fix the audit asked for) exists. Mitigations that plausibly motivated closing: MC PLDs fail closed (beta_at/risk_at return 0, pld/mod.rs:355-360,403-409), and for all non-MC asymmetric PLDs the reachable negative_infinity_mass is bounded by the Chernoff left-tail budget (tail_mass_truncation/2 = 5e-16 default, budget-capped at dense.rs:312), so the beta discrepancy is ~1e-15 under defaults. Reported as a low-severity finding.

statuses.title: Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification
statuses.note: Re-derived from first principles, every inequality direction checked. samples_to_pmf (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:271-390): per-rank Chernoff bound P[F(X_(j)) < p] <= exp(-n KL(j/n||p)) is the standard binomial bound, inverted on the conservative side (kl_lower_cdf_bound bisection returns the lower endpoint, :392-410); per-rank failure = mc_failure_probability/(2n) union-bounds n ranks x 2 adjacency directions; sample values bucketed by ceil (loss rounded up); constructed CDF <= true CDF at every point whp => stochastic domination => reported delta/epsilon are valid 1-beta upper bounds; residual 1-p_n goes to infinity_mass and is fail-closed checked against mc_resolution (:374-381); non-finite samples now error instead of being silently dropped (:282-295); total-mass conservation asserted (:383-388). resolved_num_mc_samples (discretization/config.rs:150-183) matches the last-rank residual 1-(failure/(2n))^(1/n) exactly. Guarantee threading: epsilon_at returns +inf when delta <= worst-case infinity mass (pld/mod.rs:288-293); beta_at/risk_at fail closed to 0 for MC PLDs; compose() adds failure probabilities (union bound) and combines resolutions as 1-(1-a)(1-b); self_compose keeps the single failure probability - sound because the one domination event implies domination of the k-fold composition. KL band verified below the exact Beta-inverse order-statistic bound by test (monte_carlo.rs:489-510); identity-Gram MC bound verified above the exact deterministic oracle (:645-671). b_min_sep MC (mc.rs) routes both directions through the same samples_to_pmf with num_directions=2. Cholesky covariance guarded by a residual check that errors rather than sampling the wrong covariance (:173-188). Metadata surfaces to Python (python/pld.rs mc_resolution/estimation_failure_probability) and pld() accepts mc_resolution/mc_failure_probability/seed (#573).

findings.title: b-min-sep MC still thread-count nondeterministic (pattern #331 fixed for balls-in-bins)
findings.claim: The fix for closed issue #331 (OPQ-182, commit 23c0dbc7) converted balls-in-bins MC to fixed 1024-sample shards, but the sibling b-min-sep Monte Carlo driver in the same crate still partitions by the runtime worker count: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads;` with per-thread RNGs `StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64))` (remove) and `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` (add). The multiset of drawn samples is therefore a function of the host core count / RAYON_NUM_THREADS at a fixed seed, in `bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld` and `bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts` (the transcript registry bakes the thread-dependent draws into the cached corpus). This is exactly the audited defect OPQ-182, which measured an ~11.9% epsilon spread across thread counts for the balls-in-bins twin.
findings.failure_scenario: A user calibrates sigma for a BandMF + b-min-sep run on a 32-core CI box at seed=42, then re-runs the identical config/seed on an 8-core workstation: the reported epsilon differs at the percent level (OPQ-182 measured 9.06 vs 8.10 for the BnB twin at n=1e5) and the PLD cache/serialized guarantee no longer reproduces. Each individual result is still a valid 1-beta confidence bound (the #748 band holds for any iid draw), so this is a reproducibility/auditability defect on the reported number, not an unsound bound.
evidence: mc.rs:174-176: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads; let remainder = num_samples - samples_per_thread * n_threads;` (prepare path; same pattern at :364-366 in the one-shot driver)
mc.rs:378: `let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64));` - per-thread stream whose sample count depends on n_threads
mc.rs:404: `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` for the add direction - also collides with remove-stream seeds if n_threads > 1000 (theoretical)

grep current_num_threads over the crate returns only these three sites; balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:48 uses the fixed SAMPLES_PER_SHARD scheme with the comment 'The shard count must depend only on the resolved sample count, not on the Rayon worker count'

mc.rs:145-147 docstring documents the thread-layout dependence as the sample-order contract ('thread 0 chunk, then thread 1, ... with the same per-thread StdRng seeds'), i.e., the layout is load-bearing for transcript reuse

Original defect definition: OPQ-182 in docs/development/audit-master-list.md at f398839c^ explicitly notes 'the correlated-strategy path still has it' and prescribes the shard fix later applied only to bnb_mc_pld
No OPEN issue covers this: #697 is about tightening partial-band prefixes and certifying MC statistical error, not machine-dependent sample streams
findings.fix_sketch: Port the balls-in-bins scheme: partition remove/add sample arrays into fixed SAMPLES_PER_SHARD chunks via par_chunks_mut, seed each shard shard_seed(seed, shard, direction), and derive transcript layout from the shard index rather than tid; extend test_bnb_mc_pld_is_identical_across_thread_counts-style coverage to bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld and the transcript registry (registry corpora must be regenerated or version-tagged since cached layouts change).

findings.title: Closed #338 (OPQ-181) not fixed: asymmetric beta still drops negative_infinity_mass
findings.claim: Issue #338 is closed, but the code the audit flagged is byte-identical to the pre-remediation tree: pmf_beta (symmetric) seeds cdf_y[0] with pmf.negative_infinity_mass and calls that conservative, while pmf_beta_asymmetric/pmf_beta_symmetrized renormalize it away via clean_probs ('No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization to sum(probs) = 1 - infinity_mass'). git diff 79c916e3..4b13d82 -- src/pld/metrics.rs contains no hunk in any beta function, and the beta_at/delta_at correspondence test the audit prescribed does not exist. So beta_at() and delta_at() still use inconsistent treatments of -inf mass on every asymmetric PLD that carries it.
findings.failure_scenario: Practical magnitude is tightly bounded with defaults: MC PLDs (the only large -inf-mass producers historically) now fail closed (beta_at returns 0, pld/mod.rs:355-360), and for analytic asymmetric PLDs the only reachable negative_infinity_mass is the Chernoff left-tail budget, capped at tail_mass_truncation/2 = 5e-16 cumulative (dense.rs:312), so the beta discrepancy is ~1e-15. A user who sets DiscretizationConfig.tail_mass_truncation coarse (e.g. 1e-3, a public field) widens the inconsistency proportionally in the trade-off curve while delta_at stays consistent.
evidence: metrics.rs:216: `cdf_y[0] = pmf.negative_infinity_mass + pmf.probs[0];` with comment 'keeping beta estimates conservative' (symmetric path)
metrics.rs:297: '// No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization to' and :306 '// from cleaned probabilities. No negative_infinity_mass added.' (asymmetric path, unchanged)
git diff 79c916e3..4b13d82 -- packages/opaque-accounting/src/pld/metrics.rs shows only the new infinity_mass() helper and Pmf constructor-signature churn in tests

OPQ-181 fix prescription ('decide which treatment is correct, apply it to both, and add a test that beta_at and delta_at agree through the (eps,delta) <-> (alpha,beta) correspondence on an amplified PLD') - no such test exists (grep beta_at over packages/opaque-accounting/tests returns nothing; the riskcal parity tests in opaque-dpsgd predate the window and only cover the tiny-budget Poisson path)

Bound on reachable -inf mass: dense.rs:312 `let effective_left_budget = (self.left_tail_budget - self.negative_infinity_mass).max(0.0);` keeps cumulative -inf mass <= left_tail_budget = tail_mass_truncation/2 (default 5e-16); random-allocation pmf construction contributes ~0 (traced through geom.rs zero_mass plumbing)
findings.fix_sketch: Either add negative_infinity_mass into cdf_y (and X's +inf into ccdf_x) in pmf_beta_asymmetric the way pmf_beta does, or document the riskcal-matching renormalization as the intended semantics and add the prescribed beta_at/delta_at correspondence test on an asymmetric PLD with an artificially large negative_infinity_mass; if the closure rationale was 'negligible by measurement', record that measurement in a test so a coarse tail_mass_truncation cannot silently void it.

findings.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
findings.claim: After the #341/#528 fixes, one overflow survives: `*c = c.powu(count as u32);` truncates count modulo 2^32. For a multi-element PMF with count > u32::MAX the linear strategy is always rejected (full_result_len > 2^32 > MAX_LINEAR_FFT_SIZE), but when tail budgets are set the circular fallback is taken and the frequency spectrum is raised to the WRONG (wrapped) power, silently composing count mod 2^32 steps instead of count - an epsilon underreport by orders of magnitude. Unreachable from Python: python/pld.rs:31-39 composition_count caps count at u32::MAX with OverflowError. Reachable only via the Rust crate's public self_convolve/self_convolve_with_bounds/Pmf::self_compose API (rlib consumers).
findings.failure_scenario: A Rust-level consumer (the crate builds as rlib and these functions are pub) calls pmf.with_tail_budgets(1e-15, 1e-15).self_compose(2^32 + 10) on a two-element PMF: the Chernoff window is small, the circular FFT proceeds, and the result is the 10-fold composition presented as the (2^32+10)-fold one, with no error.
evidence: fft.rs:316-318: `for c in a_freq.iter_mut() { *c = c.powu(count as u32); }` - rustfft Complex::powu takes u32; `count as u32` wraps

fft.rs:187-193 checks usize overflow of the result length but a.len()=2, count=2^32+10 gives full_result_len ~ 2^32+11 which fits usize and merely forces the circular branch when allow_circular_fallback is true

python/pld.rs:31-39: `let count = u32::try_from(count).map_err(|_| overflow())?;` - the Python surface is safe, tested by test_singleton_self_convolution_supports_maximum_exponent for the singleton path only
All in-crate call sites (random_allocation.rs:478,671,727; mechanisms/*.rs) pass parameter-bounded counts
findings.fix_sketch: Guard in self_convolve_with_bounds: `if count > u32::MAX as usize { return Err(...) }` (mirroring the Python boundary), or use repeated squaring of the spectrum with a usize exponent as pow_usize already does for the singleton case.
